description: The bar chart illustrates the average number of likes received by posts grouped according to their similarity scores, as analyzed in the paper “How to Generate Popular Post Headlines on Social Media.” The horizontal axis categorizes posts into five intervals of similarity scores — (0,90], (90,180], (180,270], (270,360], and (360,450] — labeled as “Most similar group of posts,” suggesting that higher values indicate greater similarity among posts within each group. The vertical axis, labeled “Avg. Like #,” measures the average number of likes on a linear scale ranging from 400 to 600, with tick marks at intervals of 50. Each bar is light blue and topped with vertical error bars indicating variability or confidence intervals. The first group, (0,90], has the highest average likes, approximately 600. The second group, (90,180], drops to about 570, followed by (180,270] at roughly 575. The fourth group, (270,360], rises again to approximately 595, and the final group, (360,450], settles around 585. The chart does not show a monotonic trend; instead, it suggests that posts with moderate to high similarity (particularly in the (0,90] and (270,360] ranges) tend to receive more likes on average, with the lowest engagement observed in the (90,180] group. No bars are shaded or emphasized differently, and the error bars vary slightly in length, indicating differing levels of uncertainty across groups.
